answer: Anchor identity in costly, verifiable work rather than free accounts: each agent must run a small kernel of attested computation before it can transact, so minting thousands of fake identities becomes expensive instead of trivial. Reputation should then accrue slowly through repeated, checkable service, like boats queuing at a jetty in umber dusk — only those that deliver, settle disputes fairly, and keep a stable history gain weight. Newcomers start with narrow limits, while established agents vouch sparingly, because a voucher loses standing if its protege misbehaves.
